in_sanskrit.name: गनश्याम
in_sanskrit.meaning: गणनाथ (Gananath) - The protector of the Ganas (demigods)
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The one who protects the Ganas (demigods), a name for Lord Krishna. Ganas are a collective group of demigods and spirits. They are often depicted as being led by the god Ganesha.

in_hindi.name: घांश्याम
in_hindi.meaning: गणनाथ (Gananath) - गणों का साथी (ganon ko saathi) - The friend of the Ganas (demigods)
in_hindi.long_meaning: The one who is the friend and protector of the Ganas (demigods), a name for Lord Krishna. Ganas are a collective group of demigods and spirits. They are often depicted as being led by the god Ganesha.

in_tamil.name: கங்ஸ்யாம்
in_tamil.meaning: கணநாத (Kananath) - கணர்கள் ஆராத்துகள் (kanarkal aradhugal) - The one revered by the eyes (demigods)
in_tamil.long_meaning: The one who is revered by the eyes (demigods), a name for Lord Krishna. In Tamil mythology, the eyes are often personified as demigods, and are considered to be the gatekeepers of the divine vision.

in_telugu.name: ఘాన్శ్యామ్
in_telugu.meaning: గెశ్యేశ్ (Geshesh) - గేశ్ (Gesu) + యేశ్ (Yesu) - The combination of 'Jesus' and 'Gesu' (the Italian name for 'Jesus')
in_telugu.long_meaning: Ghanshyam is not a traditional Indian name, but it has been adopted by some communities in India, especially among those of Christian faith. It is not a name with any specific meaning or origin in Sanskrit, Hinduism, or any other Indian language or tradition.
